- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md:Implementation Steps > P1 > step 5 (deterministic branch), Constraints > "Security" paragraph, line 158-163 region | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The deterministic-branch comment embeds the editor script's stderr tail (last 20 lines, capped at 4 KiB) directly in the PR comment without requiring sanitization of secrets that may appear before the script's scrub step.
  WHY: Any precondition failure between script entry and the scrub step can leak secret-valued environment variables into a public PR comment.

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md:Implementation Steps > P1 > step 4 (editor-step wrapper, ~line 297 region) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Step 4 does not specify the exact bash composition for stderr capture, exit-code recording, and portable tail truncation.
  WHY: Under `set -euo pipefail`, an implementation deviation can prevent the exit code and elapsed seconds from being recorded, so the deterministic branch never fires.

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md:Implementation Steps > P2 > step 14 (cache save/restore path rewrite), Constraints > §15 paragraph | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Step 14 changes cache paths while claiming keys and restore-keys are unchanged without specifying how run identity and cache path interaction are preserved.
  WHY: Depending on whether run identity remains in the key or path, cache hit rates can collapse or restored files can be extracted into nonexistent paths.

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md:P2 > step 14 (hydrate/stage copy), Risks & Mitigations > "Staging directory copies add a few seconds per run" | severity=high | confidence=4

  PROBLEM: Step 14 makes the staging directory `${RUNNER_TEMP}/review-state/pr-${PR_NUMBER}/` shared across concurrent runs of the same PR.
  WHY: Concurrent `rm -rf` and `cp -a` operations can clobber or read another run's staged ledger entries and resume markers.

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Implementation Steps > P1 > step 5 (deterministic branch), Constraints > "Security" paragraph, line 158-163 region
  Problem: The deterministic-branch comment embeds the editor script's stderr tail (last 20 lines, capped at 4 KiB) directly in the PR comment. The "Security" paragraph claims the comment "carries bash diagnostics only" because the script scrubs GH_TOKEN before any model launch — but the precondition failures the branch targets can fire AFTER the script's early env-load and BEFORE the scrub step (e.g., a `set -u` guard at line 26 fires before any user-defined scrub, and a custom error message in that window could echo `$OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`$OPENAI_API_KEY`/`$HF_TOKEN`/etc.). The plan names GH_TOKEN scrubbing but does not require a sanitization pass over the captured tail before posting, so any secret that the script has not yet scrubbed can be embedded verbatim in a public PR comment.
  Why it fails at runtime: any precondition failure between script entry and the scrub step will leak whatever secret-valued env vars the script has loaded into stderr; the deterministic comment will then publish those values on the PR.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=4

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Implementation Steps > P1 > step 4 (editor-step wrapper, ~line 297 region)
  Problem: Step 4 prescribes `bash "${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/review_apply_fixes.sh"` with `2> >(tee -a "${EDITOR_SCRIPT_STDERR_TAIL_FILE}" >&2)` and `|| editor_script_rc=$?` but does not pin the exact bash composition. Under `set -euo pipefail` (per `review_autofix.yml:3829,3870`) the `|| editor_script_rc=$?` only attaches to the immediate prior command; placing the process substitution on a separate line breaks the capture and re-triggers set -e exit before the rc is recorded. The "truncate the tail file to its last 20 lines" step likewise lacks a concrete portable idiom (`sponge` is not a POSIX tool, raw `tail | mv` is racy under concurrent writers). Step 4 must spell out the exact one-liner so the implementer cannot accidentally reintroduce the unobserved-failure path this PR is trying to fix.
  Why it fails at runtime: any deviation from the intended composition silently reverts to today's behaviour (exit code and elapsed seconds remain unrecorded), and the post-step's deterministic branch can never fire.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=4

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Implementation Steps > P2 > step 14 (cache save/restore path rewrite), Constraints > §15 paragraph
  Problem: Step 14 changes every cache `path:` to `${REVIEW_STATE_CACHE_DIR}/<sub>` but claims "Keys and restore-keys unchanged". The current cache config (`review_autofix.yml:2080-2083`) embeds the run-specific workspace directory inside the key itself; if that embedding is not also rewritten, the new `path:` becomes a *different* archive under the *same* key prefix. The plan needs to spell out which of (a) the key suffix, (b) the restore-keys, (c) the path: is the source of run-identity, because the §15 paragraph claims zero behavioural change beyond path-and-staging-copy while the actual hit rate will collapse if the key still encodes run-id. The plan currently treats this as obvious, but the cache key/path interaction is the load-bearing piece.
  Why it fails at runtime: if the key embeds run-id, every run creates and restores its own cache namespace (today's behaviour) and the per-PR staging directory is dead weight; if the key is run-independent but the path: still encodes run-id, the restore extracts into a path that does not exist.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=3

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md
  Line or code reference: P2 > step 14 (hydrate/stage copy), Risks & Mitigations > "Staging directory copies add a few seconds per run"
  Problem: Step 14 makes the staging directory `${RUNNER_TEMP}/review-state/pr-${PR_NUMBER}/` shared across every concurrent run of the same PR (the workflow can fire `pull_request.synchronize` plus a `workflow_dispatch` from the stall poller at the same time). The `rm -rf` in "Stage review state for cache" will wipe a parallel run's freshly staged files mid-run; the `cp -a` in "Hydrate review state from cache" will read whichever files happened to land last. Today's behaviour (per-run path in the cache key) avoids the contention by construction; the new design reintroduces it without acknowledging the race. The plan should either keep a per-run suffix inside the staging directory or document an explicit non-overlap guarantee (e.g., gate hydrate/stage on `github.run_attempt`).
  Why it fails at runtime: two in-flight runs of one PR will silently lose ledger entries and resume markers to whichever run's "Stage review state for cache" executes last.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=4

- docs/plans/review-autofix-deterministic-editor-failure-resume-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Implementation Steps > P2 > step 10 (helper signature), Tests > "P2, unit" toleration list
  Problem: The helper tolerates a missing `progress_fingerprint=` line but does not specify what `AUTOFIX_RESUME_PROGRESS_FINGERPRINT` should be exported as when every matching comment predates the new field. The plan says "the partial-finalize comment gains a `progress_fingerprint=` line" (step 12) but never says what the resume-from-comments fallback exports when that field is empty — leaving `no_progress` detection (which the partial-finalize evaluation depends on per the current runtime) free to either succeed or fail depending on the helper's default. The contract test pins the field name but not the empty value.
  Why it fails at runtime: `no_progress` would mis-fire (or under-fire) on a run whose only matching comment is an older one, marking the PR for a fresh resume round when no progress information exists.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=3
